answer: Each earning identity locks a bond and registers one exclusive transit canyon: a dedicated BGP prefix only it may announce. During the published nadir of the nightly traffic trough, the registry drops a one-shot raven token down that prefix and requires a live, latency-bound reply signed with the key sealed in the bond. A shared prefix, a reused token, or a late reply is merged into one farm and the bond burns. Fielding N aliases therefore costs N exclusive canyons, N isolated announcers, and N attendants awake in the same nadir window, which a single operator cannot staff at once.
